title: Free ChatGPT has ads now. Here is what switching them off costs you. (off day, approved by Krish 17 Nov)
experiment: A trade-off scale as the recurring device: every card after the cover shows what you give up against what you get, so the cost of each switch reads in one glance (meant to make the choice land faster than a list of settings).

five_whys.q: Why does a free ChatGPT user care?
five_whys.a: Free ChatGPT now shows sponsored cards under some answers in the countries where OpenAI runs ads.

five_whys.q: Why are there ads at all?
five_whys.a: Most people use the free plan, and running it costs OpenAI a fortune, so ads pay for it.

five_whys.q: Why don't people switch them off?
five_whys.a: The off switch is buried in settings and nobody has said what it costs you.

five_whys.q: Why is the trade-off wider than ChatGPT?
five_whys.a: Free AI is following free search and social media: you pay with attention unless you pay with money or features.

five_whys.q: Why should a business person act this week?
five_whys.a: Staff on free plans see ads beside work answers; a team should choose its plan on purpose, not by default.

explains.temporary chat: a chat ChatGPT forgets as soon as you close it (card 5)
